# Billing System Migration Rollout Plan
## 40,000 Users — Old and New Systems Running in Parallel

## Overview

This plan migrates 40,000 users from the legacy billing system to the new billing system in three named phases, using a dual-run architecture where both systems remain live and reconciled throughout the migration. The old system is retained fully operational through every phase and is only addressed for retirement after all user migration work is complete and verified.

---

## Phase 1: Pilot (5% of users — 2,000 users)

**Entry criterion:** New billing system has passed a full parallel-run reconciliation test against the old system for 30 consecutive days on synthetic/internal test accounts, with zero unresolved invoicing discrepancies, and rollback tooling (ability to revert a migrated account back to the old system) has been tested successfully on at least 50 test accounts.

**Scope:** Internal employees, opted-in low-risk customers, and accounts with simple billing profiles (single subscription, no active disputes, no multi-currency or enterprise contracts).

**Activities:** Migrate accounts in small daily batches (e.g., 200–300/day). Run both systems in shadow mode where feasible — new system processes billing, old system continues generating parallel invoices for comparison only (not sent to customer). Daily manual reconciliation review.

---

## Phase 2: Expansion (30% of users — 12,000 users)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 1 completed with fewer than 0.5% of migrated accounts requiring manual billing correction, no critical (Sev1/Sev2) incidents attributable to the new system in the final 14 days of Phase 1, and support ticket volume for migrated accounts within 10% of the baseline rate for non-migrated accounts.

**Scope:** Broader mix of customer segments, including moderate-complexity accounts (multiple subscriptions, standard discounts/coupons). Enterprise, high-value, and legally sensitive accounts (e.g., regulated billing, active legal holds) remain excluded from this phase.

**Activities:** Increase batch size (e.g., 1,000–1,500/week). Introduce automated reconciliation alerting in addition to manual review. Begin customer-facing communication about the migration for accounts scheduled in Phase 2 and beyond.

---

## Phase 3: General Availability / Final Migration (65% of users — remaining ~26,000 users)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 2 completed with fewer than 0.3% of migrated accounts requiring manual billing correction, cumulative revenue-impacting discrepancies across Phases 1–2 fully resolved and under $0 net customer-facing financial impact outstanding, and engineering/support capacity confirmed for full-scale batch size (on-call staffing plan approved for the duration of Phase 3).

**Scope:** All remaining accounts, including complex enterprise contracts, multi-currency accounts, and any accounts held back from earlier phases. Highest-complexity and highest-value accounts are migrated last, in the final sub-batch of this phase, with a dedicated white-glove review.

**Activities:** Full-scale batch migration (e.g., 5,000–8,000/week, tapering to smaller batches for the final high-complexity accounts). Final reconciliation sign-off per account before the last batch is marked complete.

**Note on decommissioning:** The old billing system is kept fully running and untouched through all of Phase 3. Decommissioning, disabling, or deleting the old system is explicitly deferred to a separate, subsequent **Phase 4: Legacy Decommission**, which begins only after a minimum 60-day post-migration parallel-run and audit period confirms 100% of the 40,000 accounts are correctly billing on the new system with no open reconciliation items.

---

## Risks

RISK: Billing discrepancies between old and new systems cause customers to be overcharged or undercharged | Run mandatory parallel shadow-billing and automated reconciliation for every account for at least one full billing cycle before cutting over customer-facing invoicing | Billing Engineering Lead
RISK: Migration batch job fails partway through, leaving accounts in an inconsistent state split across both systems | Design migration as atomic per-account transactions with automatic rollback to old-system-of-record on any failure, and checkpoint/resume support for batch jobs | Platform/Infrastructure Lead
RISK: Customer payment methods or subscription states fail to sync correctly, causing failed charges or duplicate charges | Require dual-write validation with checksum comparison on payment method and subscription data before an account is marked migration-complete | Data Migration Lead
RISK: Support team is overwhelmed by a spike in billing-related tickets during a phase, delaying issue detection | Pre-train support staff per phase, staff on-call rotations sized to batch volume, and gate phase entry on confirmed support capacity | Customer Support Manager
RISK: Regulatory or contractual billing terms (e.g., tax handling, enterprise SLAs) are not correctly replicated in the new system for complex accounts | Hold all enterprise/regulated accounts to the final sub-batch of Phase 3 with dedicated legal/finance sign-off before migration | Compliance & Legal Lead

---

## Halt Criteria (Metrics)

The rollout must be immediately paused (no further accounts migrated to the new system) if any of the following occur during an active phase:

- **Billing error rate exceeds 1.0%** of migrated accounts in any rolling 24-hour window (defined as an invoice or charge amount differing from the reconciled expected value).
- Payment failure rate for migrated accounts exceeds baseline (old-system) payment failure rate by more than **2 percentage points** over a rolling 7-day window.
- Any single incident causes **customer-facing financial impact exceeding $10,000** in aggregate before detection.

On halt, no accounts move to the next phase or batch until root cause is identified, a fix is deployed, and the affected batch is re-validated through reconciliation.

---

PHASES: 3
